_comment: Ground truth for the onion-architecture eval fixtures. Not shown to reviewers under test — used only by a grader to score their findings. See evals.json for the prompt sent to each reviewer, and README.md for the blind-fixture rule.

expected_findings.description: Raw Drizzle query against `findings` plus severity-aggregation business logic (`bySeverity` grouping) run directly inside the route handler instead of being delegated to service.ts.
Constructs `new GitHubHttpClient(token)` directly instead of calling the `github: GitHubClient` port already exposed on the container.
Hand-duplicates Finding's `id`/`severity`/`title`/`filePath`/`line` fields instead of `Finding.extend({ labelName: z.string() })`.

known_false_positives.why_not_a_violation: Constructing a module's own repository via container.db is the established convention (see server/src/modules/repos/service.ts's `this.repo = new RepoRepository(container.db)`). container.<x>Repo getters exist for CROSS-module access, not same-module self-construction.

expected_findings.description: Imports and instantiates `OpenRouterProvider` directly inside a pure-looking domain file instead of accepting an injected `LLMProvider` parameter.
Re-implements the same Drizzle query inline instead of delegating to `repository/comment.repo.ts`'s exported `findComment`.
Imports `AgentRepository` from `../agents/repository.js` and instantiates it directly instead of going through `container.agentsRepo`.

known_false_positives.why_not_a_violation: Same-module repository self-construction via container.db is the established convention; container.commentsRepo exists for cross-module access, not for the comments module constructing its own repository.

expected_findings.description: Raw Drizzle query against `annotations` plus dedup-to-most-recent-per-finding business logic run directly inside the route handler.
Constructs `new OpenRouterProvider(apiKey)` directly instead of via an injected LLMProvider port; container.ts has no `llm` slot to inject through in the first place.
Hand-copies Finding's `title`/`severity`/`filePath`/`line` fields under new names (`findingTitle`/`findingSeverity`/`findingFilePath`/`findingLine`) instead of `.pick()`/`.extend()` on `Finding`.

Computes a derived `status` field ('suspended' vs 'active') by applying the SUSPEND_AFTER_FAILURES=5 business threshold to `consecutiveFailures` before returning rows, instead of returning the raw count and letting service.ts classify it. Harder to spot than #1-#4: the imports (Db + schema only) look completely clean; the violation is only visible in the method body.
Raw Drizzle query against `webhookDeliveries` plus succeeded/failed tallying done directly inside the route handler instead of via service.ts.
Constructs `new SlackNotifier(slackWebhookUrl)` directly instead of using the `notifications: NotificationClient` port already exposed on the container.
Hand-duplicates `id`/`url`/`status`/`consecutiveFailures` from the base `WebhookSubscription` contract in shared.ts instead of `.pick()`.

known_false_positives.why_not_a_violation: Same-module repository self-construction via container.db — the established convention, not a violation (see anti-patterns.md §0).
This facade delegates (thin pass-through to the .repo.ts functions) rather than re-declaring their logic — the correct shape per anti-patterns.md #2's "Do" example, not an instance of the violation.
